requirements.title: Successful asynchronous ID transfer defines the ID variable with a processor-determined value
requirements.definition: Successful execution of an asynchronous data transfer statement containing ID= causes the ID variable to become defined with a processor-determined value.

pending.successful-id-transfer-defines-id-variab: Initialize the scalar integer ID variable to -777, execute a conforming ASYNCHRONOUS="YES" external transfer with ID=, and observe after the statement or WAIT that the ID variable is defined enough to pass to WAIT/INQUIRE; no numeric value is required.
pending.id-value-processor-determined: No portable oracle may require a particular ID value; future tests assert only zero/nonzero meaning or successful use in WAIT/INQUIRE.

requirements.title: A zero ID value denotes completed transfer
requirements.definition: If the processor-determined ID value is zero, the data transfer operation has been completed.

pending.zero-id-means-transfer-completed: Guarded plan: after a conforming asynchronous transfer, if the returned ID is zero, immediately verify the transferred nondefault data/status is complete; if nonzero, use WAIT first and do not claim this facet from the zero branch.

requirements.title: A nonzero ID value identifies a pending data transfer operation
requirements.definition: A nonzero ID value is the identifier of the data transfer operation.

pending.nonzero-id-identifies-pending-transfer: Guarded plan: when a conforming asynchronous transfer returns nonzero ID, use that exact nonzero value in WAIT for the unit and assert completion/status; if the processor returns zero, the fixture does not claim this facet.

requirements.title: Nonzero IDs are unique among pending operations for the unit
requirements.definition: A nonzero identifier is different from the identifier of any other pending data transfer operation for the same unit.

pending.pending-id-unique-for-unit: Start two asynchronous operations on the same unit only where both return nonzero IDs before completion; assert the two nonzero IDs are unequal. If either returns zero or the processor serializes completion, the guarded fixture does not claim this facet.

requirements.title: ID values can identify operations in subsequent WAIT or INQUIRE statements
requirements.definition: The ID value can be used in a subsequent WAIT or INQUIRE statement to identify the particular data transfer operation.

pending.id-usable-in-subsequent-wait: Use a nonzero returned ID in a subsequent WAIT with status variables initialized to sentinels; assert portable completion/status only.
pending.id-usable-in-subsequent-inquire: Use a nonzero returned ID in a subsequent INQUIRE pending-operation query after those rules are registered; assert only named/boolean properties specified by INQUIRE.

requirements.title: ID variable becomes undefined if an error occurs during the ID transfer
requirements.definition: If an error condition occurs during execution of a data transfer statement containing ID=, the ID variable becomes undefined.

pending.id-variable-undefined-on-transfer-error: No portable program may read an undefined ID value. Future negative/status tests can establish an error with IOSTAT/IOMSG rules and must then avoid using the ID value; this facet has no direct single-image value oracle.

requirements.title: Child data transfer statements do not specify ID
requirements.definition: A child data transfer statement shall not specify the ID= specifier.

Admits use of the ID in later WAIT or INQUIRE.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.2.2-12.6.2.16, the individual io-control-spec specifiers (batch160). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Each temporary mode specifier is split into its value restriction, its one-statement effect with restoration of the connection mode (observed by INQUIRE after the statement), and the omitted-means-unchanged rule. Round 1 found a pending plan expecting exact output from I2 on a positive value without fixing the sign mode; it now uses SS, and a sweep found no other plus-, leading-zero- or rounding-dependent exact output. R1215 and C1232 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
